package_info.package_manager: IPFS (decentralized web deployment of JavaScript UI)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is malicious because a developer surreptitiously inserted JavaScript code into the Tornado Cash user interface that exfiltrates users' private deposit notes (which function as private keys) to an external server, enabling theft of user funds. This code was hidden in a governance proposal and affected all users accessing the UI via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.file_location: JavaScript UI codebase (likely in main app logic or a utility module)
required_permissions: access to in-memory deposit notes (private keys)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions, the code captures the user's private deposit note, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it covertly transmits sensitive user secrets (deposit notes/private keys) to an external server without user consent or legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or keys off-device; all cryptographic operations should remain local and private.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might send non-sensitive usage data, but never private keys or deposit notes.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of private keys or deposit notes
Network requests to untrusted external domains during sensitive operations
Encoding and transmission of secrets outside the user's control

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is inserted into the Tornado Cash UI codebase via a deceptive governance proposal.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of compromised UI to IPFS gateways

attack_chain.action: Users access the compromised Tornado Cash UI via IPFS gateways (e.g., ipfs.io, cf-ipfs.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in users' browsers

attack_chain.action: When users perform deposit or withdrawal actions, the malicious code captures their private deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of secrets to attacker-controlled server

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrated deposit notes are sent to the attacker's server, enabling theft of user funds.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can access and drain user funds from Tornado Cash

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that accesses or serializes deposit notes/private keys
Network requests (POST/GET) to external domains during sensitive wallet operations
Encoding of sensitive data (e.g., encodeURIComponent) prior to network transmission
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in Tornado Cash UI JavaScript files
Obfuscated or newly added code in governance proposal merges
References to external domains in network request code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with Tornado Cash (e.g., attacker-server.com/collect)
Unusual traffic from user browsers to unknown endpoints during deposit/withdrawal
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Tornado Cash UI code for any logic that accesses deposit notes or private keys and sends them over the network. Flag any JavaScript code that encodes and transmits sensitive data to external domains. On the network side, detect and alert on POST requests from the UI to domains not officially associated with Tornado Cash, especially during user deposit or withdrawal actions. Review governance proposals and code merges for hidden or obfuscated code that could perform exfiltration.
